title: Give it a special Tony- I’m not even joking #Broadway #TrishaPaytas #...
transcript: So this was the most insane thing I've ever experienced. Like, within the first 20 minutes of the show, Trisha Paytas goes back in time, invents Broadway, and then changes American history forever by giving John Wilkes Booth the idea to kill Abraham Lincoln. That's how the show starts. And then, of course, you have the performances by Sutton Foster, Ben Platt, Rachel Zegler, all of whom are amazing. I was a little bit disappointed that Joy Woods did not get her own song, but I did love the Playbill outfit. And we did get to hear a little bit of her voice at the end. And speaking of the end, that medley of Trisha going through all of the Broadway shows was, like one of my favorite things that I have seen in a while. But honestly, my favorite part of the whole show was that not only was Trish getting her Broadway dream, but so many others, too. I loved that pretty much everyone in the ensemble was making their Broadway debut and that they also got a little moment to shine and take it all in. And then you have the director, who is making his Broadway directorial debut. Uh, the choreographer is also making her debut as a choreographer. It made what is objectively a very silly evening also feel really special and meaningful. And honestly, I'm not even joking. I think they should do this every Monday at the Saint James. Get four different Broadway Guest stars every show and let it run forever.
classificationReason: Creator attended the show and shares first-hand opinions about performances (Sutton Foster, Ben Platt, Rachel Zegler, Trisha Paytas), choreography, the ensemble's Broadway debuts, and the director's debut — all hallmarks of Boop! The Musical.
